premises.text: Doctors make bad treatment decisions because they lack a way to share clinical experience; static reference tools and ad-hoc texts do not feed experience back into the system
premises.evidence_span: Good doctors, like me and Mark, wind up making bad decisions because we have no way to share our experience

premises.text: SharePractice ranks treatments by doctor upvotes/downvotes with clinically relevant dosing detail and peer comments explaining choices
premises.evidence_span: these treatments are actually ranked by doctors upvoting and downvoting these treatments

premises.text: Doctors can follow expert peers and contribute votes so they both consume and participate in the curated experience
premises.evidence_span: I got the information I needed, and I was actually able to participate in the process

premises.text: In-product share to doctor contacts generates structured invitations that viral-acquire new verified physician users
premises.evidence_span: Share Practice generates the email for you. Hey, Andrew wants to know how you treat a UTI, click here to respond

premises.text: A proprietary medical ontology reconciles terminology variance across diagnosis and treatment databases
premises.evidence_span: SharePractice built a proprietary medical ontology that took multiple databases, treatment databases, diagnosis databases, put them all together

premises.text: The platform uniquely captures why doctors choose treatments—data valuable in the analytics market that does not exist elsewhere
premises.evidence_span: we're getting data that doesn't exist anywhere

domains.name: doctor experience sharing and treatment ranking

value.text: Patients get better treatment because share practice puts collective doctor experience in every doctor's pocket
value.evidence_span: share practice puts a million doctors in every doctor's pocket, and you're going to get the benefit of all of that experience

secondary_value.text: Unique why-prescribed analytics data for the healthcare analytics market
secondary_value.evidence_span: the most valuable customer in a $10 billion analytics market

causal_links.evidence_span: Viral model is baked right in, and it's working beautifully

notes: UTI demo flow treated as illustration of P2/P3. Global collaboration vision folded into value. Analytics market coded as secondary_value; primary patient-facing value is best treatment via shared experience.
